Using the KVL document, write a program that reads a KVL block and answers one lookup.
Input: the first line is N, the number of KVL lines that follow. Then N lines of KVL. The last line is the key to look up. Output: the value for that key, or MISSING.

KVL – the Key-Value Line format (version 1)
KVL is a tiny configuration format used by the (made-up) Linda deployment tool.
1. A KVL block is a sequence of lines. Each line is one of: - a blank line (ignored), - a comment: the first non-space character is '#' (ignored), - an entry: KEY = VALUE. A line that is not blank, not a comment and contains no '=' is invalid and is ignored.
2. Entries - The key is everything before the FIRST '=' sign; the value is everything after it. So "url = a=b" has the key "url" and the value "a=b". - Spaces and tabs around the key and around the value are removed. - Keys are case-insensitive: "Port", "PORT" and "port" are the same key. - If the value starts AND ends with a double quote ("), the two quotes are removed: title = "Odoo Dev" gives the value Odoo Dev. Quotes inside the value are kept.
3. Repeated keys If a key appears more than once, the LAST entry wins.
4. Lookups Looking up a key uses the same case-insensitive rule. Looking up a key that is not defined gives the special result MISSING.
Example: # server settings Port = 8069 host=localhost PORT = 8019 Looking up "port" gives 8019; looking up "HOST" gives localhost; "user" gives MISSING.

import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().split("\n") n = int(lines[0].strip()) data = {} for line in lines[1:1 + n]: s = line.strip() if not s or s.startswith("#") or "=" not in s: continue key, value = s.split("=", 1) key, value = key.strip().lower(), value.strip() if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == '"' and value[-1] == '"': value = value[1:-1] data[key] = value query = lines[1 + n].strip().lower() if len(lines) > 1 + n else "" print(data.get(query, "MISSING"))
